items.text: Nicolas Jackson has four goals in five Premier League games since joining Villa, two of them against Manchester City last Saturday, while Fulham's 40m pound striker Gonzalo Garcia has gone seven games without scoring, the Guardian notes. Jackson is Edward's and Garcia is Big Ben's, and Unai Emery's knowledge of Jackson from their Villarreal days is the thing the piece credits for the difference.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Nottingham Forest are in the bottom three after a 1-1 draw at Ipswich, the Guardian reports, with Neco Williams scoring from Daniel Munoz's overlapping run while Morgan Gibbs-White, who started the season well for chances created, was crowded out by Ipswich's packed midfield. Williams and Gibbs-White are both Edward's, and the piece says better finishing is what Oliver Glasner's side need.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Edward spent the day binning Leno, Williams and Horníček, who returned 8 apiece in the best eleven of the week, and took Pickford, Porro and Verbruggen on the strength of nothing anyone has seen yet. The Return of the Djedi has found a way to be kneejerk without any help from Marcus.

Big Ben made five waiver claims today and one of them is McBurnie, of Hull, which is a lot of new names for the man who sells himself as the last word on ball knowledge. He is 89 off the lead and has apparently decided the answer was never at Arsenal after all, only that nobody told the Arsenal fan.

Justin, 8 clear, spent the day adding Odegaard and Gyokeres to a squad that already held Raya and White, so tomorrow's Liverpool v Arsenal puts four of his men on one side of it. Stach and Brobbey went out to make room, and neither will be missed by anyone, least of all the scoreboard. It is a lead protected the traditional way: by owning the whole of one club and then hoping.

The page logged thirteen waiver moves today and none of them were Marcus's, the same Marcus who sold a winger the day after two good games, and who is 8 behind with Tzolis at a 75 percent chance of playing. Either the kneejerk has been put to bed, or the luck has told him to sit tight, and for Marcus it has never been easy to tell which of the two is doing the talking.

Chelsea go into the 12.30 against Manchester United without James (knee, out until January), Joao Pedro (thigh, no return date) and Lacroix (hamstring, no return date), and Martinez is out with a jaw injury until 8 November, the Guardian's predicted lineups report. That is Robert's James and Martinez gone from the same back line, Marcus's Joao Pedro on the sidelines, and Small Ben's Lacroix with them. Man Utd lose Sesko to a shin injury until January, which is one more name off Robert's list.

source.title: Premier League team news: predicted lineups for the weekend action

items.text: Arsenal travel to Anfield on Sunday with Tzolis out with a hamstring injury until 7 November, and Saka (thigh) and Saliba (back) both listed as injured with no return date, according to the Guardian's team news round-up. Tzolis is Marcus's, Saka is Robert's, and neither is likely to be there when Arsenal kick off.

source.title: Premier League team news: predicted lineups for the weekend action

items.text: Bruno Fernandes is expected back in Manchester United's starting lineup at Chelsea after he was an unused substitute in the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth, the Guardian reports. He and Michael Carrick held clear-the-air talks this week after he criticised the tactics in the Champions League defeat at Como. Big Ben owns him.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Gonzalo Garcia has gone seven games without scoring for Fulham, and the Guardian calls his form concerning as Alvaro Arbeloa's side, who went six league games without a win to start his reign, travel to Aston Villa tonight. Big Ben has Gonzalo in his fifteen, and Villa's Nicolas Jackson, who has scored four in five, belongs to Edward.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Team news, 15:00 kick-offs: Leeds XI at Bournemouth is confirmed. Edward: Muharemovic and Calvert-Lewin start. Big Ben: Trafford starts. Justin: Bogle starts. Robert: Wilson starts. No confirmed sheet found yet for Bournemouth, Brentford, Forest, Hull, Ipswich, Man City, Brighton, Coventry or Sunderland, so those players are not counted.

source.title: Daniel Farke makes two changes for Bournemouth clash

items.text: Team news, Spurs v Palace (17:30 kick-off): Marcus (Kinsky), Justin (Marmoush), Big Ben (Van Hecke, Kudus) and Robert (Solanke, Mateta) all start. Small Ben has Van de Ven starting but Maddison on the bench, and Edward's Pedro Porro is also on the bench.

source.title: Confirmed line-ups: Spurs vs Crystal Palace

items.text: Mateta finished the afternoon on minus two and in the dressing room early, banned until 2 December, which makes him the second thing about Robert this month to leave early with no plan to come back. The other is the hairline.

Big Ben's day was built by Van Hecke at Spurs and McBurnie at Hull, neither of them anything to do with Arsenal, the club he follows with such conviction, who play at Anfield tomorrow with Konsa in his eleven. Fifty-six already, and not a point of it from the club he claims to know.

Small Ben has a fight coming, and Suzuki, who he owns, spent Saturday putting one in his own net: that is the whole boxing plan, hitting yourself before the other man gets round to it. Thiago did bring him 9, which is the bit he will mention. The rest he will leave out.

Justin spent Friday loading up on Arsenal and spent Saturday with none of them kicking a ball, while Haaland took 90 minutes against Brighton to return 2 points and left the nets exactly as he found them. Four of his eleven play at Anfield tomorrow, so the day is not over, which is the best thing anyone can say for it.

Liverpool v Arsenal is the only fixture of the gameweek still to come, at Anfield at 16:30. Arsenal have not won there since 2012 and arrive four days after going out of the Carabao Cup to League Two Fleetwood, while Liverpool have won five on the spin under Iraola. Still waiting: Raya, White, Odegaard and Gyokeres (Justin), Gabriel, Saka and Mosquera (Robert), Calafiori (Marcus), Rice and Madueke (Small Ben), plus Virgil, Gakpo and Isak (Small Ben), Barcola (Justin) and Wirtz (Big Ben) on the Liverpool side.

source.title: Anfield, intensity, rotation - how Iraola is improving Liverpool

items.text: Brighton won 1-0 at the Etihad on Saturday, three days after losing to City on penalties in the Carabao Cup, and Bart Verbruggen made seven saves to give them a fifth clean sheet in six league games. That is Edward's goalkeeper, and Marcus (De Cuyper) and Justin (Vuskovic, Boscagli) took defensive returns off it too. City's owners had the opposite afternoon: Justin has Haaland and Gvardiol, Robert has Cherki, O'Reilly and Ndiaye, and Marcus, Small Ben, Edward and Big Ben each hold a City player of their own.

source.title: Verbruggen spreads belief as Brighton continue to impress

items.text: Estevao had not started a Premier League game this season before Saturday, and against Manchester United he had six shots, created three chances and had two goals chalked off, one for a marginal offside, before leaving to a standing ovation after 86 minutes. Robert owns him and the page has him on 3 points, with no goal to show for it. Morgan Rogers (Big Ben) scored the one that mattered for Chelsea, in a 2-0 win.

source.title: Returning Estevao brings X-factor to strikerless Chelsea

items.text: Lisandro Martinez was sent off at Stamford Bridge after two fouls in one minute and 23 seconds turned a decent Manchester United away performance into a 2-0 defeat, and BBC's United reporter says Carrick did not look at him as he walked off. United's owners in this league are Robert (Yoro, Sesko), Big Ben (Bruno Fernandes) and Marcus (Mbeumo), who all now have a manager under pressure to answer to.

source.title: Martinez's 'inexplicable' 83 seconds cost Man Utd and Carrick

items.text: Team news, Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30). Big Ben: Jacquet, Wirtz, Konsa, Havertz all start. Small Ben: Virgil, Gakpo, Isak, Madueke, Rice all start. Edward: Timber starts. Marcus: Calafiori, Tzolis start; A.Becker not in the squad. Justin: Barcola, Raya, Odegaard start; White, Gyokeres on the bench. Robert: Gabriel starts; Mosquera on the bench, Saka not in the squad.

source.title: Team news: Confirmed Liverpool line-up v Arsenal

items.text: Robert's gameweek is 13 points and four players who returned nothing, Saka and Mosquera among them, and he sits 154 off the top. The gap to first place is now receding faster than his hairline, which had a head start of several years and is still being overhauled.

Marcus and Edward end Sunday level on 446, three clear of Justin, with Marcus's Dewsbury-Hall and Edward's Tarkowski and Barry all waiting on the Everton game. De Cuyper and Evanilson carried Marcus; Guehi, Mukiele and Joao Pedro each turned up and delivered nothing, a body of work the Jobacus archive would recognise, except that this time nobody paid to watch the outdoor scenes. Somewhere a creepy priest in Spotlight is still taking notes.

Edward has called Big Ben a biased Arsenal fan with no ball knowledge, and then Konsa took 10 and Havertz 9 for him at Anfield while Bruno, his usual lifeline, gave 2. The bailout came from the club he supposedly knows nothing about, which is either ball knowledge or luck, and Big Ben's 68 is the biggest gameweek in the league either way. It still leaves him fifth, because he started the week a long way behind.

Small Ben has nobody left to play and sits 36 behind the leaders, with Isak, Virgil and Gakpo adding five points between them against the Arsenal he also owns half of. Three rivals still have players to come and he has a finished gameweek and a view of the top of the table from a long way below it, which for a man of his height is the usual angle.

Kai Havertz scored after 16 minutes at Anfield, his first goal in 10 appearances, and Arsenal won there for the first time since September 2012 with Liverpool finishing without a shot on target, the Guardian reports. Havertz is Big Ben's, as is Konsa behind him; Calafiori and Tzolis (Marcus), Raya and Odegaard (Justin), Gabriel (Robert) and Madueke and Rice (Small Ben) were all in the same win. Madueke was booked, and Virgil van Dijk was heard in the tunnel saying he should have had a second yellow.

source.title: Arsenal hold on for first league win at Liverpool since 2012 after Kai Havertz pounces early

items.text: Andoni Iraola said Liverpool will tell their players to go down in the box in future after Isak was denied a penalty at Anfield. Isak stayed upright while Jurrien Timber held a handful of his shirt as Barcola's cross came in, and the VAR did not step in; a second claim, Tzolis holding Gakpo, was reviewed and rejected. "We have to tell them to go down because they're not going to call it otherwise," Iraola said. Isak and Gakpo are Small Ben's, Barcola is Justin's, Tzolis is Marcus's, and Timber is Edward's.

source.title: 'We have to tell them to go down': Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial for Liverpool

items.text: Everton host Newcastle tonight at 20:00 UTC, five days after beating them in the Carabao Cup, a game Jack Grealish missed after Everton said he had breached club discipline, the Guardian reports. It is the last fixture of the gameweek, and it is still to come for Edward's Tarkowski, Barry and Pickford, Big Ben's Branthwaite, Marcus's Dewsbury-Hall and Small Ben's Osula, who scored at Selhurst Park on 25 October.

source.title: Grealish could have been Everton's poster boy of a new era. Now his career is in limbo

items.text: Team news, 20:00 kick-off, Newcastle v Everton: Newcastle's confirmed XI is out and Osula (Small Ben) starts. Everton's teamsheet was not available at a permitted source yet, so Branthwaite (Big Ben), Pickford, Tarkowski and Barry (Edward) and Dewsbury-Hall (Marcus) are left out of the counts.

source.title: Confirmed line-up: Elanga in for Everton

items.text: Robert's Monday gets a minus sign, courtesy of Mateta on -2, and four more of his eleven (Saka, Mosquera, Martinez and Sesko) played and gave him nothing. Thirteen points off a whole gameweek is the sort of return a man gets for not touching his team since the summer, and the hairline is going in the same direction at the same speed.

Edward spent September telling anyone who would listen that Big Ben has no ball knowledge, and Big Ben has answered with 74, the biggest score of the gameweek, with Van Hecke on 15 and McBurnie on 12. Edward still leads the league, which is the only reason the biased Arsenal fan has not yet had to stand in front of the room and explain himself.

Marcus began the gameweek 2 behind Edward and ends it 17 behind, which is what happens to a man who runs on luck every week the day the luck takes a Sunday off. Dewsbury-Hall and Evanilson got him nine apiece and it still was not enough to make anybody ask where Edward's cushion came from.

Small Ben takes 40 from the gameweek, sits 51 off the top, and Thiago on 9 is the only man in his eleven who looks like he trained for it. The upcoming fight is going to be the same story: plenty of enthusiasm and no plan for the second round, and nobody in the room has ever called him big.

Thierno Barry tapped in the winner at St James' Park last night, his second goal against Newcastle in five days and his eighth of the season, which already matches his whole of last year. BBC Sport call him Everton's only recognised senior striker since Beto left for Fiorentina, so Edward owns the most indispensable man at his club. The goal began with a Branthwaite flick-on, so Big Ben had a hand in it from the back, and Jaissle says Barry fouled Schar in the build-up.

source.title: From nightmare debut season to Everton hero - Barry's revival

items.text: Newcastle were jeered off again after losing at home to Everton, and BBC Sport note nobody in the Premier League has lost more home games in 2026 (seven) and that they have gone 14 home league games without a clean sheet, a club record. Hornicek let a routine shot squirm under him for the winner. Small Ben's Osula plays for a side Jamie Carragher calls flat and boring at home.

source.title: Jeers again as home woes continue - Jaissle has big problems at Newcastle

items.text: Edward went from 21 behind to two clear in a single gameweek, on the back of Verbruggen, Barry, Jackson and an Everton spine that keeps turning up, and managed it while leaving 18 on the bench. Return of the Djedi is a grand name for a man holding first place by a margin one Pickford howler could undo, and the Force has not yet been seen to help anybody with a two-point lead.

Justin started the gameweek in first and finished it twelve behind in third, on 31, with Haaland on 2 and Gyokeres on 1 up front. The two most famous strikers on the squad sheet gave him three points between them, which is roughly what a man gets for spending the week confident about his attack.

Robert was given a full pint last week and left it. This week he was given eleven players and a whole Saturday and finished on 17, 165 behind the top, so the pattern is at least consistent: whatever is put in front of him, he declines to see it through.

Marcus is two off the top and the squad shows exactly how: De Cuyper and Evanilson on 9 each, then Mbeumo and Foden on 1, with Guehi, Mukiele and Joao Pedro on nothing. Each of them presumably arrived after two good games somewhere, which is the Elanga method, and the method remains undefeated at finding the third game.

Sunderland are sticking with Regis le Bris, BBC Sport report, despite one win from nine and the bottom spot after Saturday's defeat at Coventry. Club sources believe he can turn it round, and Chelsea visit on Sunday. Robert's keeper Roefs and Marcus's Mukiele are the Sunderland men in the league, and Marcus, Edward and Big Ben all own Chelsea players on the other side of it.

source.title: Bottom club Sunderland to stick with manager Le Bris

items.text: Troy Deeney's BBC Sport team of the week has a heavy league flavour: Bart Verbruggen (Edward) for keeping Brighton in it at Manchester City, Ezri Konsa (Big Ben) for a beast of a display in Arsenal's 1-0 win at Anfield, and Rice (Small Ben), Van Hecke and McBurnie (both Big Ben) in the headline selection too.

source.title: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?

items.text: Big Ben has spent two months leaning on Bruno Fernandes to haul him out of trouble, and in the gameweek where he outscored everybody, Bruno gave him 2. Nobody was rescued. A centre-back and a Hull striker did it, which tells you the whole reputation was built on a man who turns up to rescue the team and then watches somebody else do it.

Small Ben left 12 points on his bench this week, which is a lot of dugout for a man who talks about his upcoming fight as if preparation were optional. Same instinct in both: pick the wrong eleven, trust the gloves, find out in the second round what the bench knew all along. At least Harvey Price could say he had a plan.

Crystal Palace have lost their appeal against Jean-Philippe Mateta's red card from the defeat by Tottenham, so Robert's striker, who left GW9 on minus 2 after being sent off in the 13th minute for a late challenge on Micky van de Ven (Small Ben's), now misses the Liverpool game, the trip to Coventry on 21 November and Hull at home on 29 November, BBC Sport report. He stays available for Palace's Europa League matches.

source.title: Palace lose appeal against Mateta red card

items.text: Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, lost his appeal, and is banned for three Palace games, which makes him the fastest-receding thing in Robert's squad, a title that for once is not held by the hairline. The difference is that Mateta at least went through the motions of an appeal. Robert, who has not made a transfer in recent memory, will presumably leave him in the eleven to serve the ban with dignity.

Marcus has Guehi, Mukiele and Joao Pedro all sitting on nothing from last gameweek and still ended it two points off the top, which is the kind of absolution usually only available from a man in a cassock who has been asked to look after the choirboys in the Spotlight sense. Three blanks forgiven before he has even said sorry. The Jobacus channel is presumably already filming the penance, outdoors.

Justin finished the gameweek twelve off the lead, and the first thing he did was sack Gyokeres, a striker who gave him 1 point, along with Schade, and bring in Cunha and Gonzalo. It is the move of a man who has looked at a league table and decided the problem is the people in it rather than the one picking them. Cunha's new club hosts Villa next, so the first review of the new regime is already booked.

Virgil van Dijk called Liverpool's defending "not sustainable" after they led 2-1 in Istanbul and lost 3-2 to Fenerbahce, all three goals coming from set-pieces. It is the first time Liverpool have conceded three or more in three major European games in a row, and they have lost their last two. Small Ben owns Van Dijk, Gakpo and Isak, Big Ben has Wirtz and Jacquet, Marcus has A.Becker and Justin has Barcola, so a leaky Liverpool is nearly everyone's problem.

source.title: Defensive problems not sustainable - Van Dijk

items.text: Jack Grealish will not be available for Everton against Coventry tonight at 20:00 UTC, David Moyes confirmed on Thursday, with the on-loan City midfielder still sidelined after a breach of club discipline and last seen in the 17 October defeat by Chelsea. Moyes would not give a plan for his return. Edward (Tarkowski, Barry, Pickford), Big Ben (Branthwaite) and Marcus (Dewsbury-Hall) all have Everton players going out tonight.

source.title: Grealish unavailable again for Everton

items.text: Unai Emery is close to agreeing a new Aston Villa contract after talks with the club's hierarchy on Wednesday, with the length and finances still being settled. The extension would give him even more say over Villa's long-term development. Edward (Jackson, Manzambi), Small Ben (Suzuki) and Big Ben (Konsa) all hold Villa players, none of whom will mind the man picking the team staying put.

source.title: Emery close to agreeing new Aston Villa contract

items.text: Team news, Everton v Coventry (20:00): Edward has Pickford, Tarkowski and Barry all starting. Marcus has Dewsbury-Hall starting. Small Ben has Mykolenko starting. Big Ben has Branthwaite starting; Coventry's sheet was not available, so Awoniyi is unconfirmed.

source.title: Everton Team Revealed To Take On Coventry

items.text: Return of the Djedi led by 2 this morning and leads by 14 tonight, and Edward is already carrying himself like the council has asked him to take a seat. Barry did the work, Tarkowski turned up for it, and the man who picked them has eight more to come tomorrow and the posture of someone who has never had to defend a lead before.

Big Ben's Friday was Branthwaite's 3 points and a Coventry striker who spent 86 minutes offside for 2 more, which makes the best news of his night a defender being cleared to play. Ten of his eleven kick off tomorrow, so he gets to be a different man, which is the hope he has had every Friday since September.

Small Ben took 8 from Mykolenko, signed Rayan off the free agents the same day, and presumably felt the 62-point gap to the top shrink by a waiver claim's worth. It is a lot of ambition from a man whose title chances are measured in the same unit as his height.

Robert has not had a single player kick a ball this gameweek, which for a man who barely touches his squad is the closest he gets to a clean sheet: nothing he picked has had the chance to let him down yet. All eleven go tomorrow, 186 off the lead, and the hairline and the league position can get back to receding in step.

Thierno Barry scored twice as Everton came from behind to beat Coventry 3-1 on Friday night and move up to fifth, with Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall adding a thunderous strike hours after learning he had been left out of Thomas Tuchel's England squad. It is the night Edward's Barry banked his points and Marcus's Dewsbury-Hall banked his, and David Moyes now has two wins in a row to point at.

source.title: Barry scores twice as Everton fight back to beat Coventry

items.text: James Trafford says sitting on the fringes at Manchester City last season was "horrendous" and that he had to play regularly for his mental wellbeing, which is why he left for Leeds in the summer. Gianluigi Donnarumma, who arrived from Paris St-Germain less than six weeks after City brought Trafford back, is Small Ben's goalkeeper; Trafford is Big Ben's, and Leeds host Tottenham at 12:30 UTC today.

source.title: 'I had to play regularly for my mental wellbeing' - Trafford

items.text: Oliver Glasner says Nottingham Forest had "too much Woodstock" and need more military: trust and respect, in his words, are the two values he will not negotiate on. Forest are 19th, winless and goalless at home in the league, and host Manchester City at 17:30 UTC tonight, which is a fixture Edward's Gibbs-White, and everybody holding a City player, will be watching.

source.title: Forest need balance between Woodstock and military - Glasner

items.text: Newcastle were booed off after losing 1-0 at home to Everton on Monday, a fourth defeat in six Premier League games, and Matthias Jaissle admitted he understood the reaction. They are at Fulham at 15:00 UTC today, so Small Ben's Osula goes into it with his side in poor form, while Marcus's King and Justin's Gonzalo are on the home side.

source.title: Jeers again as home woes continue - Jaissle has big problems at Newcastle

items.text: Team news, Leeds v Spurs (12:30): Edward has Muharemović, Calvert-Lewin and Pedro Porro all starting. Big Ben has Trafford, Van Hecke and Kudus starting. Justin has Bogle and Marmoush starting. Marcus has Kinsky starting. Robert is hit: Wilson and Solanke are both on the bench.

source.title: Confirmed line-ups: Leeds vs Spurs

items.text: Team news, 15:00 kick-offs: Newcastle's confirmed eleven is out and Small Ben's Osula starts at Fulham. The Arsenal, Hull and Fulham sheets were not available when this was written, so Edward, Marcus, Robert, Justin, Big Ben and Small Ben's other players at those clubs are not covered yet.

source.title: Confirmed line-up: Four changes at Fulham

items.text: Big Ben's eleven has 12 between them tonight while his bench has more, and the loudest of it is Trafford's 10 for Leeds, so the best goalkeeping in the league this gameweek was done by a man watching from the dugout. Havertz gave him 2 and the Arsenal ball knowledge the league keeps saying he lacks, and Petrovic does not kick off until Sunday to find out what he missed.

Edward began the gameweek 2 clear and is 25 clear tonight with four of his eleven still to play, 16 of it Barry, and the man who explains every other manager's week as luck will have the winter to explain Barry as a long-term conviction. Somebody should ask him in March which of the two it was.

Justin sacked Gyokeres for Gonzalo and Cunha, Gonzalo has returned 2, and Cunha does not kick off until Sunday, so the review of the new regime is still waiting for the evidence to arrive. Bogle gave him 7 and Tzolakis 6 from the bench while Haaland, in the eleven, brought back 2, which is a squad being run with great confidence by the man at the wrong end of it.

Robert has 21 from Saturday and Cherki's 9 and Gabriel's 8 are nearly all of it, while Saka and Mosquera played the same Arsenal match as Gabriel and returned nothing. A side with all the effort at the back and nothing at the front, which is also the hairline, and in both cases the manager has stopped doing anything about it.

Tottenham are set to complain to Pro Ref after Jayden Bogle escaped a red card for catching Mathys Tel on the back of the ankle with his studs in Leeds' win on Saturday. VAR reviewed it but referee John Brooks was never sent to the monitor, and former assistant referee Darren Cann called Bogle fortunate. Justin owns Bogle, so a belated retrospective punishment is the only way this costs him anything.

source.title: Tottenham set to complain to Pro Ref after Bogle escapes red card

items.text: Mikel Arteta says Noni Madueke has become a 'different' player, filling in on the right since Bukayo Saka's injury: 13 touches in the opposition box against Hull was the most by an Arsenal player in a Premier League game this season, and his shot led to the save from which Martin Odegaard scored. Small Ben owns Madueke, Justin has Odegaard, and Robert has Saka waiting to get back into the side.

source.title: Noni Madueke has become a 'different' player, says Mikel Arteta, as winger finds new level of creativity and efficiency

items.text: Estevao had the most shots and touches in the opposition box in Chelsea's game with Manchester United, and Xabi Alonso said he 'has had the best response, to show he deserves more'. It remains to be seen whether he starts at Sunderland today (14:00 UTC), though his chemistry with Cole Palmer might tempt Alonso. Robert owns Estevao and Edward owns Palmer.

source.title: Estevao ready for more Chelsea minutes under Xabi Alonso after reminder of his threat against Man Utd - The Radar

items.text: Team news, Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30): Marcus (Mbeumo), Justin (Cunha), Big Ben (B.Fernandes) and Robert (Yoro) all start for United. Robert's Sesko is not in the United squad named (not in the XI or on the bench). Villa's full eleven was not available at a permitted source, so Edward (Manzambi, N.Jackson) and Small Ben (Suzuki) are left out of the counts.

source.title: Harwood-Bellis starts against United

items.text: Edward began the gameweek 2 clear and ends it 17 clear, and 16 of that was Barry in an Everton shirt doing the lot on his own. The Return of the Djedi has been rebuilt as a one-man tribute act, and Marcus has just spent a Sunday finding out which of the two of them is the opening act.

Mateta and Šeško both played today and brought home nothing between them, 5 of Robert's eleven in all, which makes his front line the only thing about him receding faster than the hairline. It is a rare gift to be last, quiet about it, and still be leaving by the front.

Thiago got himself sent off for minus two and is banned until 5 December, and Small Ben still has to look up 73 points to find the leader. At that height it is a lot of looking, and the one man in the squad who has been told to sit down is the only one with a plan.

Marcus began the gameweek 2 behind Edward and ends it 17 behind, which is what happens to a man who runs on luck every week the day the luck takes a Sunday off. Dewsbury-Hall and Evanilson got him nine apiece and it still was not enough to make anybody ask where Edward's cushion came from.

Bruno hauled 10 for Big Ben today, from the bench, alongside Trafford's 10, so the man who needs Bruno to bail him out had him in the building and left him in the dugout. A bench with 24 on it and an eleven that needed it: classic Arsenal fan reading of a football match.

Manchester United twice came from two goals down to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa, Patrick Dorgu levelling in the 96th minute, and still go into the international break 18th and without a league win since 30 August. Michael Carrick, asked about walking away, said "That's not going to happen." Justin (Cunha), Marcus (Mbeumo), Big Ben (B.Fernandes) and Robert (Sesko and Yoro) all have United men to look at, and the next fixture is Anfield on 22 November.

source.title: Bizarre & thrilling theatre as Carrick in limbo with Man Utd in drop zone

items.text: Brighton beat Brentford 2-0 on Sunday to go second, five points behind Arsenal, with six wins in seven, and Pascal Gross, who scored and created at least five chances, is the man the BBC credits for most of it. Big Ben owns Gross; Justin, Marcus and Edward all have a Brighton defender or keeper as well. Gross himself says they are not in a title race.

source.title: Are 'outstanding' Brighton now Arsenal's main title challengers?

items.text: Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 on Saturday through Enzo Le Fee's 36th-minute penalty, after Levi Colwill brought down Brian Brobbey, and the BBC had Robin Roefs rarely tested and Nordi Mukiele a huge presence at the back on his return. Robert (Roefs) and Marcus (Mukiele) both came out of it with 9, while the Chelsea players in the league, Palmer, Rogers, Neto and the rest, brought home next to nothing.

source.title: Failed to deal with Brobbey - player ratings for Sunderland v Chelsea

items.text: Robert is 192 off the lead with a front line of Mateta, Saka, Mosquera and James that all went the whole of GW10 without troubling a scorer. Saturday is the first chance to make a transfer since he last answered a message, and the smart money is on the hairline making its move first.

Justin finished second in GW10 and still found a way to feel hard done by: Gvardiol and White blanked, Haaland gave him 2, and Tzolakis and Bogle sat on the bench doing the work of men being paid to start. Running a squad this confidently and getting it this wrong takes real commitment.

Edward won the gameweek, extended the lead to 17, and still left 14 on his bench, which means the man he spends every week explaining as luck has now got his reserves out-earning half the league's eleven.
